newsitem.title: USA: US foreign crudes quiet, prices retain strength.
newsitem.headline: US foreign crudes quiet, prices retain strength.

text.p: The U.S. foreign crude scene was subdued on Wednesday amid continued strong prices, traders said.
The June spread between WTI and Brent narrowed to around $1.50-55 a barrel, down some 15-20 cents from Tuesday, but was still strong enough to sustain transatlantic activity.
A trading company was still offering North Sea benchmark Brent for about 50 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for June 10-15 arrival.
A U.S. company believed to have Brent for June 22-27 arrival, asking around WTI/Cushing minus 50-55 cents a barrel.
"There are a lot of barrels popping up," said one Texas trader.
From Africa, a U.S. company had Qua Iboe and Brass River to sell for June 20-25 arrival, asking dated Brent plus $2.05 and $2.17 a barrel, respectively, on a delivered basis, traders said.
Saharan Blend cargoes were also looking for buyers for early and late June arrival, asking around dated Brent plus $2.10 or WTI plus 25 cents a barrel.
From Latin America, offers for sweet Cusiana crude were running around $1.10 a barrel under July WTI, about 15 cents stronger than the price at which the grade was last sold.

Finally, premiums for Exchange for Physical deals eased to around six to eight cents on Wednesday, down from 12-13 cents a barrel earlier this week on revived talk of foreign crude deliveries into the NYMEX when the June contract expires on May 20, traders said.
